Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for sending the initial SIG answers. We reviewed the access-control section and have a few follow-ups before we close our assessment: 

1) SAML: Can you confirm whether Redwood supports scoped assertion audiences per SP (a per-tenant assertion audience value), or if assertions are generic across tenants? Also looking for an export of the SAML binding matrix and any recommended SP metadata examples.

2) SCIM: We need clarification on your delta / incremental sync cadence and what change-types you emit (create/update/replace/delete). Is there an SLA for SCIM sync delivery?

3) RBAC / least privilege: Please provide a role inventory snapshot (roles -> permissions) for your hosted control plane admin roles and any guidance on delegating least-privilege to customers integrating via SCIM.

4) MFA: Are there any documented exceptions for service accounts that bypass MFA? If so, how are those access requests audited?

Could you send the answers and any artifacts by COB Friday PST? If you need an extension we can adjust the timetable but would like clear expectations.

Thanks,

- Role inventory (rbac_role_inventory_20260828.xlsx): contains roles, scoped permissions, and the source-of-truth (control plane vs. customer-mapped). We include a column showing whether a permission is considered "privileged" for least-privilege guidance.

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up - MFA/service-account exceptions and SCIM SLA

Hi Olivia — adding a few specifics on MFA and SCIM reliability: 

MFA: No customer-facing service accounts bypass MFA by design. Exceptions do exist for internal pipeline/service identities and are protected by short-lived keys, scoped roles, and mandatory audit logging. When an exception is approved (rare), the workflow includes:
- Approval ticket in our internal system
- Automated alert to security ops
- Monthly exception report attached to the quarterly attestation

SCIM SLA: We do not guarantee strict delivery windows for downstream processing (depends on customer endpoint availability), but our system guarantees delivery attempts with exponential backoff for up to 72 hours. We emit delta-change events including create/update/replace/delete with timestamps and change tokens so customers can reconcile. Attaching the SCIM sync SLA PDF.

[Attachment: scim_sync_sla.pdf (pdf)]

—Sean
